pull_request.title: Migrating the snippet format to a markdown approach
pull_request.body:
# Description

As we discussed in the discord, contributing and reviewing pull request is becoming harder, largly due to the way snippets are stored.
This PR changes that by introducing a `snippets` folder at the root of the project, this folder contains folders for each languages and categories, snippets are defined with markdown files with a simple structure.

The most important commit of this PR is the first one, the second one migrates already existing snippets to the `snippets` folder, the third one re generates the json language files with the new format, and the fourth fixes issue with the code of snippets switching from an array to a continuous string.

So this PR adds three scrips and one util:
- `migrateSnippets.js` - Which generates the `snippets` folder from language files (It can be removed when we this gets merged)
- `snippetParser.js` - This is the util, it exposes function that allow for parsing the snippet folder.
- `checkSnippetFormatting.js` - Just checks the formating of the snippets using `snippetParser.js` it does not modify anything (Should be runned on commit/PR)
- `consolidateSnippets.js` - Takes all the snippets and generates the language json files under `/public/data`, also copies the icon in the right places and generates the `/public/data/_index.json` file.

## Checklist

- [X] I have tested my code and verified it works as expected.
- [X] My code follows the style and contribution guidelines of this project.
- [X] Comments are added where necessary for clarity.
- [X] Documentation has been updated (if applicable).
- [X] There are no new warnings or errors from my changes.

issue.title: Task 10: Initialize Hardhat, Run Compile, and Write `deploy.js` for Contract Deployment
issue.body:
**Description:**  
This issue involves setting up Hardhat in the project for smart contract development, running a compilation to verify the setup, and writing a `deploy.js` script for deploying the smart contract to a specified blockchain network. A screenshot of the successful compilation and deployment should be included in the submission.  

---

### **Tasks:**  
1. **Initialize Hardhat:**  
   - Run `npx hardhat` to initialize the Hardhat environment in the project.  
   - Choose "Create a JavaScript project" during setup.  
   - Install necessary dependencies such as `ethers`.  
2. **Configure Hardhat:**  
   - Set up the `hardhat.config.js` file for the desired network (e.g., localhost or a testnet).  
   - Add appropriate configurations for network connections, private keys, and gas limits.  
3. **Run Hardhat Compile:**  
   - Execute `npx hardhat compile` to ensure the setup is correct and the smart contracts compile successfully.  
   - Take a screenshot of the terminal showing the successful compilation.  
4. **Write `deploy.js`:**  
   - Create a `deploy.js` script in the `scripts` folder.  
   - Add logic to deploy the smart contract to the specified network using `ethers.js`.  
   - Include the following:  
     - Reading contract artifacts and ABI.  
     - Connecting to the specified Ethereum provider (local or testnet).  
     - Deploying the contract and outputting the deployed address.  
     - Logging errors if deployment fails.
     - Use the current network as a testnet  
5. **Run Deployment:**  
   - Use the script with `npx hardhat run scripts/deploy.js --network <network-name>` to deploy the contract.  
   - Take a screenshot of the terminal showing the deployed contract address.  

---

### **Requirements:**  
- The deployment script must be modular and reusable for future updates.  
- Include comments in `deploy.js` to explain each step of the deployment process.  
- Upload screenshots of the terminal showing:  
   - Successful compilation.  
   - Successful deployment with the deployed contract address.  

---

### **Submission Guidelines:**  
1. Pull the latest changes before pushing to the repository.  
2. Submit a pull request (PR) using the provided PR template.  
3. Include screenshots or logs of:  
   - The successful Hardhat compilation.  
   - The successful contract deployment on hardhat-network (npx hardhat node)
---

### **Resources:**  
- [[Hardhat Documentation](https://hardhat.org/docs)](https://hardhat.org/docs)  
- [[Hardhat Deploy Script Example](https://hardhat.org/tutorial/deploying-your-contracts.html)](https://hardhat.org/tutorial/deploying-your-contracts.html)  
- [[Connecting to Networks with Ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.org/v5/api/providers/)](https://docs.ethers.org/v5/api/providers/)  

Feel free to reach out on Discord for clarifications or assistance. 🚀

issue.title: Large map simulations with esmini
issue.body:
I am testing `Gemini` with larger road networks, and I encounter some problems (possibly memory leaks) as the application gets unresponsive without showing the window.

I was using the maps from the Carla simulator (https://github.com/carla-simulator/opendrive-test-files). Smaller maps (`Town01-02`) run as expected with a size of `<1MB`, but slightly larger ones (`Town03-06`) do not run even headless with a size of `>2M`. The medium-sized `Town07` with a size of `1.6MB` interestingly runs headless but not with a window. So the limit seems to be around `1MB` in terms of map filesize.

I expect super-large maps would be out of scope, but I wonder what map sizes can be realistically achieved with the current architecture. Is this a bug or an architecture limitation?

Thanks!
